prompt_en: Photorealistic single-frame environmental portrait: a random complex test concept in an orbital greenhouse at night. An adult materials scientist, her visible appearance guided only by the supplied portrait, has long center-parted dark wavy hair, dark eyes, softly arched brows, and broadly comparable facial proportions. She presents the transparent cylindrical quartz ampoule beside her visible face. Inside, a visible phase transition proceeds by nucleation and growth, forming a visible nucleation-and-growth phase transition. Show that one material specimen has a complete readable boundary that owns every phase region inside the transparent cylindrical quartz ampoule. Establish that a temperature pressure field or concentration gradient acts coherently across that same specimen from frosted copper cooling clamp to warm ceramic ring. Ensure the original parent phase remains materially legible around the emerging regions as translucent amber fluid around pale crystals. Render multiple distinct nuclei of a new phase form inside the parent material rather than as surface decoration throughout the fluid as separated pale crystal islands. Show a continuous advancing interface keeps parent and new phases simultaneously visible inside one specimen along the cold-to-warm axis. Dense frost and condensation mark the cold clamp end; the warm ring end remains clear. Waist-up documentary composition; the ampoule crosses the lower foreground with her face above on the same focal plane. Neutral practical light, realistic glass refraction, clean unlabeled surfaces, amber-copper-cyan palette.
